To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the anomaly of the (2, O) Schwinger model is nonvanishing, and that the one-loop effective action is finite and nontrivial.
the (2,O) Schwinger model is an anomaly free model, and that the 1-loop corrections of the effective action are given by the anomaly of the current.
The anomaly of the chirally coupled supercurrent is equal to minus the anomaly of the current associated with the gauge field.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: (1) The anomaly of the chirmal supercurrent is calculated by the supergraph technique, and the result is shown to be consistent with the anomaly cancellation condition in the (2,0)-Schwinger Model.
the study of quantum corrections to a (2,0)-supersymmetric model of gauge theory.
the study of quantum-mechanical corrections to a supersymmetric gauge theory, which are shown to be nonperturbative.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the (2,O) model is free from the problems of the (2,1) model and is a good model for a supersymmetric gauge theory.
, at least for the case at hand, the anomaly of a conserved supercurrent and the 1-loop effective action are not independent quantities.
the 1-loop effective action in the superspace formulation of the (2,0) Schwinger model does not exhibit any quantum anomaly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the case of the (2,0) Schwinger model, the quantum corrections to the (2, 0)-supersymmetry are not sufficient to generate the mass of the gauge boson.
, for the first time, a (2,O)-superfield theory has been studied in detail at the one-loop order and the results obtained are in agreement with the known ones in the (2,O) case.
the (2,O) model, in spite of its nonrenormalizability, can be quantized consistently.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quantum-mechanical (2,O)-gauge model is not asymptotically free.
the quantum corrections to the classical action of (2,O)-superfield theories are governed by the same mechanism as in the ordinary (2,0)-model.
the (2,O) supersymmetry of the model is preserved at one-loop order.
